content: Business invariants and history belong to one named bounded context. Contexts integrate through stable IDs and published contracts; desktop, web, and KiCad-facing shells stay thin composition roots. Avoid ownership-free core, models, or utils modules.

title: Keep SQLite roles physically and logically separate
rationale: The team-authoritative database, each desktop replica, generated KiCad projection, and external read-only databases serve different consistency and authority roles. Synchronize records and regenerate projections atomically; never multi-writer-sync SQLite files.

title: Use PocketBase as the sole team backend
rationale: PocketBase is selected for its maturity, documentation, authentication, realtime, file, migration, hook, job, and backup capabilities. Domain rules remain in application-owned interfaces and protected server-side commands, but the repository will not build an alternate-provider adapter or comparison harness. Pin every PocketBase version and checksum, rehearse upgrades, preserve a canonical export, and prove blank-environment recovery.

content: Each frontend seed owns its full feedback loop: add semantic and accessibility assertions, automate the critical journey, and take deterministic screenshots of distinct states. Inspect the screenshots and differences, fix every material issue, and rerun. Screenshot review adds to behaviour tests. Accept baseline changes explicitly, never just because a test changed.

name: Restore PocketBase through an S3-compatible blank-environment drill
description: Test backup and recovery with isolated MinIO buckets. Seed records and files, back up and checksum, destroy the PocketBase state, restore into a blank pinned instance, and compare records, files, hashes, rules, migrations and versions. pb_data backups exclude files stored in S3, so those need their own restore proof. MinIO proves S3 behaviour, not AWS-specific configuration.

outcomes.test_results: 16 Rust tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, manifest check, and source-immutability gate passed; independent review PASS

name: Loss-detecting fixture boundaries fail closed
description: Fixture and import oracles read path syntax as text, not with the host's path rules. They accept only exact-case regular files inside the root, and reject traversal, links and reparse points before probing. They report discovery failures, keep SQLite NULL apart from empty text, and report field-level differences beside byte identity.

title: Develop and validate natively on Windows for now; defer the Docker lab
rationale: The user chose Windows-native work for the time being so Docker is not a dependency. The Rust workspace gate (cargo test, fmt, clippy -D warnings, the import fixture check) must pass on Windows. The Docker AFK lab stays in the repo but isn't run or extended until kicad-parts-c748 resumes it.

description: On Windows, core.autocrlf=true turned LF catalog files into CRLF on checkout. The import oracle had recorded byte hashes from one such checkout, so it failed on other checkouts and on Linux.
resolution: .gitattributes sets '* text=auto eol=lf' and '-text' on the data folders, so the working tree matches the committed bytes on every OS. The manifest's byte hashes now describe committed bytes. Tests that change serialization flip the line ending instead of assuming CRLF.

content: Guard execution environments with exhaustive allowlists, not word filters. Examples: the normalized Compose policy, per-image Dockerfile contracts (bases, downloads, checksums, apt packages, RUN programs), and a single Program enum enforced by clippy disallowed-methods on Command::new. Word bans had to obfuscate their own source and still let unlisted tools through.

title: KiCad 10 is required; the app, tests and CI may run it
rationale: Users already have KiCad installed, and CI runners will too. Use the installed KiCad, mainly kicad-cli, wherever it already does the job. Test against a real KiCad 10, with a manual checklist only for what kicad-cli can't show. Never change an open design or editable library behind KiCad's back (mx-3903cc, mx-70700f).

description: tauri-driver passes tauri:options.args to msedgedriver, which treats them as browser switches. It sorts and lowercases them and turns a standalone value into its own switch, so '--data-dir C:\x' arrives as '--c:\x --data-dir'.
resolution: Desktop journeys pass launch options as --name=value. apps/desktop parses both forms and ignores unknown arguments.

title: Hold Leptos at 0.8.3 while the toolchain is Rust 1.85
rationale: Leptos 0.8.4+ declares rust-version 1.88, and its sub-crates (server_fn_macro, server_fn_macro_default) publish no rust-version, so the fallback resolver picks releases built on syn 3 that break leptos_macro 0.8.3. apps/desktop-ui/Cargo.toml pins leptos, server_fn_macro and server_fn_macro_default to =0.8.3 (and Cargo.lock follows); revisit when the toolchain moves to 1.88+.

name: Run desktop journeys on a hidden Win32 desktop
description: tooling/journey-desktop creates a run-scoped desktop with CreateDesktopW and starts tauri-driver on it inside a kill-on-close job. The app and WebView2 inherit it, so journeys show no window and take no focus. Screenshots match a visible run, and run time is the same. npm run journeys is hidden by default; --visible or JOURNEYS_VISIBLE=1 shows it.
pocketbase serve, on a data directory with no superuser, opens its installer page in the default browser. That popped up on the developer's laptop during tests.
resolution: PocketBaseServer::start in tooling/native-services takes a Superuser and always runs 'pocketbase superuser upsert' first. Services start suspended in a kill-on-close job that allows one process, so they can't launch a browser. A log with the installer banner fails the start.

description: Rust's Path::canonicalize on Windows returns a verbatim \?\C:\... path; Go reads the '?' as a glob wildcard, so go:embed patterns matched nothing and the MinIO build failed with 'pattern ...: no matching files found'.
resolution: native_services::repository_root strips the \?\ prefix (not \?\UNC\) before paths are handed to child programs.

name: Native disposable PocketBase and MinIO for tests
description: tooling/native-services reads infra/versions.lock, caches checksum-verified downloads, and runs services on random 127.0.0.1 ports in a kill-on-close job. Build MinIO with -buildvcs=false and a cleared environment, or the pinned hash matches only one commit. PocketBase 0.38 can't restore in place on Windows, so unpack the S3 backup into an empty pb_data. Wait for /minio/health/ready.

In a PocketBase JSVM route, JSON.stringify(e.requestInfo().body) isn't deterministic, because the body is a Go map with varying key order. A request hash built from it made an identical retry look like a reused correlation ID (409).
resolution: Build request hashes from validated values in a fixed order, as catalog_csv_imports.pb.js and collab_commands.pb.js do.

description: pocketbase migrate down asks 'Do you really want to revert...? (y/N)'; with stdin closed (run_hidden) it prints 'The command has been cancelled' and still exits 0, so a test that checks only the exit status passes without reverting anything.
resolution: native_services::run_hidden_with_input writes 'y\n' to stdin (still windowless, in the kill-on-close job); assert stdout contains 'Reverted <migration>' and inspect data.db (see tooling/catalog-import test the_catalog_migration_rolls_back_from_a_populated_instance).

content: Keep terminology as simple as possible for people. Use plain, everyday words and the fewest terms in the glossaries, code names, docs and UI, following the ISO 24495 plain-language skills (iso-24495-1 for text, iso-24495-code for code). When a new concept needs a name, prefer a plain phrase over a new coined term. The user asked for this on 2026-10-09.

description: In a PocketBase 0.38 JSVM onRecordUpdate hook, e.record.original() is empty for a record the same handler created and saved again. So a guard comparing fields with original() refused the CSV import.
resolution: Read the stored row with e.app.findRecordById(collection, e.record.id). e.app is the transaction, so it sees earlier writes. See infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_write_guards.pb.js.

description: PocketBase capitalises the first letter of an ApiError message and adds a full stop, so BadRequestError(`${reference} is not ...`) reached the user as 'G-pas:NOPE is not ...'. In migrations, collection.updateRule is a Go string pointer: typeof is not 'string', so string checks on it silently fail.
resolution: Start route error messages with a plain word ('the symbol g-pas:NOPE is not in the Catalog'). Convert rules with String(rule) before comparing or slicing (1791600000_catalog_edits.js down migration).

description: Under tauri-driver, msedgedriver replaces WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS with its own, and tauri:options.args reach only the app. So --force-device-scale-factor changed nothing, and at 150% scaling screenshots stayed 1920x1200.
resolution: apps/desktop takes --display-scale=N on Windows. Before Tauri starts, it appends --force-device-scale-factor=N to WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS and sizes the window in screen pixels. Journeys pass --display-scale=1 and assert 1280x800 screenshots.

name: Compare journey screenshots with reviewed baselines; re-run incomplete contrast checks
description: apps/desktop/journeys/baselines holds one approved PNG per state, taken with --display-scale=1 and --software-rendering. harness.mjs compares with pixelmatch (threshold 0.02, anti-aliasing counted) and fails above 4 pixels. --update-baselines stages new screenshots and copies them only if every journey passed. assertAccessible re-runs colour contrast on elements axe marks incomplete.

With a strict 4-pixel limit, a hidden journey run failed 9 screenshots by thousands of pixels. WebView2 had switched from GPU to software drawing partway through, changing every anti-aliased edge. No limit separates that drift from a one-character change.
resolution: apps/desktop takes --software-rendering on Windows, adding --disable-gpu and --disable-partial-raster to WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS. Journeys always pass it with --display-scale=1, and 10 of 10 runs matched.

title: Approved journey screenshots are shared across machines
rationale: User decision on 4a88, 2026-10-10. One committed set of approved screenshots for every machine, including the CI runner, which will have KiCad. Machine-specific paths are blanked out, and a committed environment file (KiCad and WebView2 versions) lets the runner say plainly when a machine differs. Not built yet (kicad-parts-4a88).

description: PocketBase capitalizes the first letter of a hook's BadRequestError message (and adds a full stop), so a message that starts with a library reference (g-Resistor_SMD:...) reached the user as G-Resistor_SMD:...
resolution: Start route error messages with ordinary words (the Footprint field lists X twice), never with a case-sensitive name; compare messages case-insensitively in tests only when the name is not first.

description: A full journey run once failed spec 03 at launch: the node test process exited with 0xC0000409 after tauri-driver logged os error 10054. The spec passed alone and in the next full run.
resolution: Treat it as a tauri-driver or msedgedriver flake: rerun the spec, then the suite, and say so. Next time, keep the driver logs from target/journeys/latest before rerunning.

description: Python edits on this Windows machine: open() defaults to cp1252 and text mode writes CRLF, so LF files turn CRLF and git warns. Bash heredocs with backticks or ${...} also break the Bash tool's quoting.
resolution: Open files with encoding='utf-8', newline='', or set PYTHONUTF8=1. If CRLF crept in, run sed -i 's/\r$//'. Write longer scripts to a file with the Write tool. In temp test repositories, pass -c core.autocrlf=false. Chain lint and commit with && under set -o pipefail, because a pipe to tail hides a failing clippy.

description: Journeys pass --disable-gpu, yet WebGL still works there: WebView2 draws it with Microsoft's software renderer (Basic Render Driver). Its pixels may differ between machines, so a 3D canvas in a shared screenshot can fail.
resolution: Hide .view3d-canvas for pixel screenshots, as journey 20 does. Check the 3D view by reading pixels and mesh names through view3dInfo(), which draws and reads in one call.

content: Decisions that are hard to reverse, surprising and a real trade-off get an architecture decision record (ADR) in docs/adr/, because the domain-modeling skill looks for them there. Each ADR names its mulch records, and mulch keeps the detail. When you change such a decision, update its ADR and its mulch records together. The user asked for this on 2026-10-17.
